We need propose a 3-step retrosynthesis for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to another phenyl ring bearing an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to phenyl with side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH (anilide). So three steps: likely disconnection at amide formation (C=O to amine), at sulfonamide formation (S-N bond), and at the α,β-unsaturated acid formation via Doebner modification (forming the double bond and carboxylic acid). So retrosynthesis:

Target -> disconnect amide: gives carboxylic acid precursor (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step1: amide coupling.

Precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid attached to phenyl-sulfonyl group: phenyl-SO2-Ph-CH=CH-COOH (with para-methyl on first phenyl). Actually the sulfonyl phenyl is the same as target's sulfonyl phenyl (p-tolyl). So we have phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl with side chain unsaturated acid.

Now step2: disconnect the double bond formation via Doebner modification: starting from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl-sulfonyl phenyl with aldehyde at para position relative to sulfonyl? Actually the side chain attaches at para position of second phenyl (the one attached to sulfonyl). The SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So the aldehyde would be at that position: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (para to sulfonyl). So we can get that aldehyde via Doebner from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (p-tolyl-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde) and malonic acid (or its derivative). So step2: Doebner modification.

Step3: sulfonamide formation: connect p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride with the phenyl bearing aldehyde (or later). So we need sulfonyl chloride precursor: p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (CH3-Ph-SO2Cl). And the other component: aniline (the phenyl ring that will later become aldehyde). Actually the sulfonamide is formed between p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) which has the aldehyde later. So we can disconnect sulfonamide to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride and the aniline (the phenyl ring with aldehyde). So step3: sulfonamide formation.

Thus three steps: (1) amide coupling, (2) Doebner modification, (3) sulfonamide formation.
